arxiv-2111-14866.creator: Fulya Kıroğlu, Newlin C. Weatherford, Kyle Kremer, Claire S. Ye, Giacomo Fragione, Frederic A. Rasio
arxiv-2111-14866.description: Abstract Many recent observational and theoretical studies suggest that globular clusters (GCs) host compact object populations large enough to play dominant roles in their overall dynamical evolution. arxiv-2404-12144.description: Abstract Modern agricultural applications rely more and more on deep learning solutions. arxiv-2410-02083.title: Sensitivity analysis of the thermal structure within subduction zones using reduced-order modeling
arxiv-2410-02083.description: Abstract Megathrust earthquakes are the largest on Earth, capable of causing strong ground shaking and generating tsunamis. Physical models used to understand megathrust earthquake hazard are limited by existing uncertainties about material properties and governing processes in subduction zones. A key quantity in megathrust hazard assessment is the distance between the updip and downdip rupture limits.

pmc-11605051.title: Evolutionary insights into the stereoselectivity of imine reductases based on ancestral sequence reconstruction
pmc-11605051.creator: Xin-Xin Zhu, Wen-Qing Zheng, Zi-Wei Xia, Xin-Ru Chen, Tian Jin, Xu-Wei Ding, Fei-Fei Chen, Qi Chen, Jian-He Xu, Xu-Dong Kong, Gao-Wei Zheng
pmc-11605051.description: The stereoselectivity of enzymes plays a central role in asymmetric biocatalytic reactions, but there remains a dearth of evolution-driven biochemistry studies investigating the evolutionary trajectory of this vital property. Imine reductases (IREDs) are one such enzyme that possesses excellent stereoselectivity, and stereocomplementary members are pervasive in the family. However, the regulatory mechanism behind stereocomplementarity remains cryptic.

pmc-12643810.title: Transcystic management of choledocholithiasis: Outcomes, factors associated with bile duct injury and implications for surgical practice
pmc-12643810.creator: Víctor Nieto Barros, Laura Alonso Murillo, Raúl Castañeda Vozmediano, Carlos García Vásquez, Santos Jiménez-Galanes Marchán
pmc-12643810.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Backgrounds/AimsCholedocholithiasis with gallbladder in situ presents a complex surgical challenge. The transcystic approach offers a minimally invasive alternative to choledochotomy; however, its adoption remains limited. This study assessed the safety, efficacy, and reproducibility of this method.MethodsThis retrospective study involved 71 patients diagnosed with choledocholithiasis and gallbladder in situ, all of whom underwent transcystic bile duct exploration at a primary care hospital.
